# Pragmatism Widens the Field of Search for God

Pragmatism[^1] has in fact no prejudices whatever, no obstructive dogmas, no rigid canons of what shall count as proof.[^2] She is completely genial.[^3] She will entertain any hypothesis, she will consider any evidence.[^4] It follows that in the religious field she is at a great advantage both over positivistic empiricism, with its anti-theological bias, and over religious rationalism, with its exclusive interest in the remote, the noble, the simple, and the abstract in the way of conception.[^5]

In short, she widens the field of search for God.[^6] Rationalism sticks to logic and the empyrean.[^7] Empiricism sticks to the external senses.[^8] Pragmatism is willing to take anything, to follow either logic or the senses, and to count the humblest and most personal experiences.[^9] She will count mystical experiences if they have practical consequences.[^10] She will take a God who lives in the very dirt of private fact-if that should seem a likely place to find him.[^11]
